header:
Date: 2026-06-18
Start: 15:00 CDT
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Alex Carter (Redwood AE), Priya Menon (Redwood SE), Liam Ortiz (Redwood Solutions); John Patel (Summit Bank, CTO), Maria Gonzalez (Summit Bank, CISO), Tom Reeves (Summit Bank, Head of Cloud Ops), Leah Brooks (Summit Bank, Product)
summary: Initial discovery on data residency and compliance needs. Summit Bank is evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment for Redwood. Primary concerns: GDPR/data residency, financial services logging restrictions, PII handling, audit logs retention, KMS/keys, SOC2/HIPAA controls, and network egress constraints. Agreed next steps: Redwood to send security artifacts and schedule SE deep dive on private/VPC architecture. Customer to provide data flow and retention policy.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
transcript:
[00:00] Alex (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro from our side, i'm alex carter, AE on the account. priya is our se and will cover private/dedicated architecture.
[00:12] John (Summit Bank - CTO): Thanks Alex, John here. We run most infra in us-east-1 but have EU presence, GDPR is a must for some products.
[00:25] Maria (CISO): Hi, Maria. Our security team needs to understand where customer data lands, retention of logs, and whether redwood keeps request transcripts. Also we have some HIPAA-bound flows.
[00:38] Priya (Redwood SE): Great, thanks. Quick overview: Redwood offers Hosted API, Dedicated reserved pools, and Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments. For data residency we commonly do either region-restricted hosting or Private with customer-managed network.
[00:52] Tom (Cloud Ops): When you say region-restricted, does that mean logs and payloads stay in the region, or just compute? We have strict rules that data for EU customers must not leave EU and we also keep derivative data for analytics but need to limit retention.
[01:06] Priya: Region-restricted hosting pins storage and compute to a region; logs and telemetry can be configured to stay in-region. For extra control, Private gives you full control over VPC endpoints and egress policies.
[01:22] Leah (Product): What's the difference in SLA/latency between Dedicated and Private? If we go Private in our VPC, will latency be worse?
[01:31] Liam (Redwood): Typically Dedicated gives the best predictability and lowest latency because we manage optimized GPU pools. Private depends on your infra — colocated private deployment can match Dedicated if network latency is low. There's a tradeoff vs operational overhead.
[01:47] Maria: Ok. Compliance: do you have SOC 2 and any HIPAA attestations? Also encryption at rest and in transit?
[01:55] Alex: We are SOC 2 Type II, and we support HIPAA controls (we have a HIPAA onboarding pack). Encryption in transit is TLS, at rest is AES-256. We integrate with customer KMS for key management on Private and Dedicated in some configs. We'll send the certs and a short HIPAA summary after this call.
[02:12] Maria: Good. For logging, we need control over retention and the ability to redact PII before logs leave our VPC. Does Redwood retain raw request transcripts on Hosted by default?
[02:23] Priya: By default Hosted stores transcripts for a limited time for debugging/analytics but we offer redaction and log-retention configs for enterprise plans. On Dedicated we can restrict retention and on Private you control logs entirely. Note: our auto redaction isn't perfect — recommend we plan a custom redaction step in your ingestion if you have strict PII constraints.
[02:41] John: What's the story for GDPR - data subject requests and right to be forgotten? If a customer asks us to delete data, can we trace and purge request logs from your side?
[02:53] Alex: For Hosted we can honor deletion requests for customer data; on Dedicated/Private you control the data lifecycle. We'll need to map out which artifacts need to be purged (training cache, KV cache, logs). Priya: also be aware of KV cache/prefix caches — those can store tokenized context and need explicit purge APIs.
[03:12] Tom: We also have a 'no-logging' requirement for certain flows, i.e., no request or prompt storage. Is that doable on Hosted?
[03:21] Priya: On Hosted it's harder; best approach is Dedicated with strict retention or Private where logs never leave your VPC. We can configure request routing so those flows go to private/dedicated endpoints to enforce no logging.
[03:37] Maria: For HIPAA, we need Business Associate Agreement (BAA). Do you sign BAAs?
[03:42] Alex: Yes, we do for qualified plans. We'll follow up with legal and include the BAA template.
[03:49] Leah: What about key management — you mentioned KMS/HSM. If we bring our own KMS, do you hold raw keys?
[03:58] Priya: You manage keys in your KMS/HSM; Redwood uses envelope encryption where the customer-managed key decrypts on the host side. For Hosted we support cloud KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) with role-based access. For on-prem/private we can support HSM. We'll send the KMS integration notes.
[04:16] John: Any limitations on models we can run in Private? We have some compliance-approved open models we want to serve.
[04:24] Priya: We support most open architecture LLMs; we do kernel selection and quantization for performance. Private deployment requires us to validate the model artifacts, but generally it's supported.
[04:36] Tom: How about audit logs? We need immutable audit trails for who invoked which route and which keys were used, with retention up to 7 years for some products.
[04:48] Alex: We provide audit logs with admin-level events, and you can export to your SIEM. Retention policies are configurable on Dedicated and Private. For Hosted, we offer configurable retention windows but long-term retention is an enterprise add-on. We'll include export options in the doc pack.
[05:04] Maria: Are there any export restrictions or egress that could cause data to leave the region due to third-party services? We use third-party monitoring and don't want telemetry to route outside EU.
[05:15] Priya: We can configure integrations to use in-region endpoints; Private keeps everything inside your network. For Hosted we have region-specific endpoints that minimize cross-region egress, but it's important to review each integration.
[05:30] John: Performance question: if we route EU traffic to a EU Dedicated pool, will that add 30-40ms vs US?
[05:38] Liam: Not typically that high. Latency is mostly network; Dedicated pools in-region should be within single-digit ms for token generation if model is the same. We can run benchmarks with a sample prompt set to measure.
[05:52] Leah: On the procurement side what's the expected timeline to pilot and then commit to Dedicated?
[06:00] Alex: Typical pilot runs 4-6 weeks to prove latency and cost. After pilot, Dedicated contracts are monthly/annual reserved. For Private onboarding add a couple more weeks for network and security review.
[06:12] Maria: On legal, we need a data processing addendum (DPA) and BAA options. Also want to ensure SOC2 reports are current.
[06:21] Alex: We'll attach DPA and SOC2. I'll also include our incident response and breach notification timelines.
[06:32] Tom: We may require IP allow-listing for API endpoints and mutual TLS for ingestion. Is mTLS supported?
[06:40] Priya: mTLS is supported for Private endpoints; for Dedicated we can do IP allowlist and VPC peering or private link depending on cloud. We'll detail options in the technical follow-up.
[06:54] John: A bit worried about telemetry — you said Redwood uses analytics. Can we opt out of user-level telemetry?
[07:02] Alex: Yes, analytics can be disabled for enterprise customers; we can also provide aggregated metrics only. We'll note that in the security pack.
[07:12] Maria: For GDPR DSARs, how quickly can you assist with searches for a user's data across logs in Hosted?
[07:20] Priya: We provide APIs and support, but response time depends on retention windows. For Hosted we'll need at least the retention window and mapping; for Dedicated/Private you can do full control.
[07:32] John: Ok. Could you outline the recommended approach for our use case? We have: consumer banking (US), EU wealth management (EU GDPR bound), and an upcoming health-benefit product (HIPAA-ish).
[07:45] Priya: Recommended: keep consumer US flows on Hosted or Dedicated US depending on latency/cost; EU wealth management should be Dedicated EU or Private in EU to ensure residency; for the health flows, use Private with BAA and strict no-logging config. Use routing and policy to send each flow to appropriate endpoint.
[08:05] Leah: What's the effort to put routing rules in place? We have a gateway that can tag requests.
[08:12] Liam: We can support routing by token or route name. If your gateway tags requests we can route based on metadata to different deployments.
[08:20] Alex: We'll include a sample routing policy and a POC plan in the follow-up.
[08:27] Maria: Anything to call out around data used for model improvement? We do not want our data used for model training.
[08:33] Alex: By default Redwood does not train models on customer data for Hosted enterprise customers unless agreed; we'll provide contractual language to prevent any model training on your data. On Dedicated/Private you control models.
[08:47] John: Great. On metrics/cost — can we get an estimate for token costs for Dedicated vs Hosted?
[08:54] Alex: We'll send a cost worksheet. Dedicated is typically lower per-token but requires commit.
[09:02] Leah: OK, next steps recap?
[09:05] Alex: Recap: Redwood to send SOC2, HIPAA summary, DPA, BAA template, KMS notes, routing policy sample, and a proposed pilot plan. Summit Bank to share data flow diagram, list of PII fields, and retention policy. We'll schedule SE deep dive on private deployment the week of 6/29.
[09:22] Maria: Sounds good. Also legal will want to review DPA and BAA; we may have follow-up questions.
[09:29] Tom: We'll try to get the data flow by 6/25.
[09:33] Alex: Perfect. Anything else?
[09:36] John: No, thanks everyone.
[09:38] Alex: Thanks all, we'll follow up via email with the docs and calendar invite for the SE deep dive.
[09:43] [call ends]
